What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item D1 is a loop strap clamp: a formed aluminum strap with a mounting hole in its tab, wrapped around a soft cushion liner that holds a pipe, hose or wire bundle.

The item's 3D model: the strap, the mounting-hole tab and the black cushion liner.
A cushioned loop strap clamp for reference — metal strap on the outside, rubber liner on the inside.

Aluminum Strap — the formed metal band that wraps the liner. The KMC marking is stamped on it.

Mounting Hole Tab — the flat end of the strap. Its 0.281″ hole takes the fastener.

Cushion Liner — black rubber inside the strap. It grips, dampens vibration and keeps metal off metal.

Reading a Part Number Like an Engineer

The part number /KMCCOL0509AL has a clear structure — a leading slash, a supplier prefix, and the catalog's own part number. This module walks through the part end to end: where it lives, what it is made of, and the paperwork behind it.

Topic T2 · Part Number Decoder

Three Key Part Characteristics

Hover over any element of the part number below to see what it means — the same way SBS reads a new item, one piece at a time.

/KMCCOL0509AL  =  5/16 LOOP STRAP CLAMP EPDM CUSH ALUM
KMC Stampings — the supplier named by the three letters after the slash.

Reading the Prefix

  1. The slash. Marks a catalog or print part.
  2. KMC. The supplier code — the first letters after the slash point to the supplier, here KMC Stampings.
  3. COL0509AL. The part number straight from the supplier's catalog.
The same item, as it appears in the SBS item record: Item #, the Customer Part # (BRP part # 293650256, active), and the item description.

5/16

Nominal clamp diameter — it matches the 0.312″ inside diameter on the item specification.

LOOP STRAP CLAMP

The part type: a formed strap that loops around a pipe, hose or wire bundle and bolts down through its tab.

EPDM CUSH

An EPDM rubber cushion liner sits between the strap and whatever it holds.

ALUM

The strap material is aluminum. The extended description adds ROHS and the supplier catalog number, KMC # COL0509AL.RoHS: EU rule limiting lead, mercury & similar substances.

Topic T4 · Material Selection

Aluminum

“ALUM” in the item description calls out the base material of the strap. Here is why aluminum is a good fit for a clamp like this.

Requirement

Material: Aluminum · Grade: Aluminum · Finish: Plain

Corrosion Resistant

Ideal for humid, marine and chemical environments.

Highly Formable

Easily molded, extruded or machined into complex clamp shapes.

Sustainable & Recyclable

Lower carbon footprint than steel; recycling requires far less energy than new production.

Aluminum — element 13, atomic weight 26.981.

The strap is only half the clamp. See what the liner adds in .

Topic T5 · Cushion Liner

The EPDM Cushion Liner

The “EPDM CUSH” in the description is the rubber liner inside the strap. It does three jobs.

Dampens Vibration

Dampens and absorbs vibrations on secured pipes or hoses — reduces noise and reduces wear.

Protects What It Holds

The cushion prevents rubbing or damage to wiring, pipes or hoses.

Stops Galvanic Corrosion

Helps prevent galvanic corrosion when installed on aluminum tubing — the liner is a barrier between dissimilar metals.Galvanic corrosion: corrosion that happens when two different metals touch in a moist environment.

A cushioned loop strap clamp for reference.

Which Cushion?

The KMC catalog lists EPDM as the standard cushion, with neoprene and silicone as optional cushions. This item's description calls out EPDM.

Topic T6 · Applications

Where Loop Strap Clamps Are Used

Anywhere something needs to be held in place without being damaged — from buildings to power lines.

Construction

In the construction of roads, bridges, buildings, etc.

Industry

In the automotive, electronics, aviation and home appliance industries.

Electric Power Operation

In dead-end points, bridges and suspension supports.

Protection

To protect cables from damage and prevent tripping hazards.

Installation

To secure and facilitate the installation of wiring, cabling, conduits, pipes and fiber optics.

Inspection Report vs. Catalog

Inspection Report

The SBS report carries the PPAP level (4), part number, description and drawing, then one row per feature. When a lot is inspected, each measured dimension is recorded against its minimum and maximum. Rows 4–8 are the caliper dimensions.

KMC Catalog Row

The same dimensions come from the supplier's COL0509 row: a nominal value and a tolerance, so nominal ± tolerance gives the report's min and max.

Click a number on the inspection report to see exactly where that dimension and tolerance comes from in the KMC catalog.

1 · Clamp Diameter – D

Ref .312 (pass / fail).
Catalog column D, Clamping Diameter: .312 ±.031.

2 · Hole Diameter – H

Min .276 / Max .286.
Catalog column H: .281 ±.005 → .276 to .286.

3 · Clamp Width – W

Min .490 / Max .510.
Catalog column W: .500 ±.010 → .490 to .510.

4 · Hole Center to End – E

Min .297 / Max .327.
Catalog column E: .312 ±.015 → .297 to .327.

5 · Hole Length – S

Min .355 / Max .395.
Catalog column S: .375 ±.020 → .355 to .395.

The report's feature / tolerance rows — the numbered pins match the catalog columns.
KMC catalog, COL0509 row (D, H, W, E, S).

Center to center (L), slot gap (F) and gage are in the catalog but are not on the inspection report. Burrs, material and surface finish / color are checked against the print and item specification, not the catalog.

Visual & Document Checks

Burrs, material (ALU / EPDM) and surface finish / color (PLN / BLK) are checked visually or against documents.

Caliper Checks

Clamp diameter .312; hole diameter .276–.286; clamp width .490–.510; hole center to end .297–.327; hole length .355–.395.

Reference

Glossary

Every code and acronym used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term's “jump” button to see it in context.

Aluminum

The strap material of this clamp: corrosion resistant, easily formed and highly recyclable.

BRP

Bombardier Recreational Products — the customer whose part number (293650256) is linked to this item.

Catalog Part

A part ordered by its supplier catalog number rather than a custom print; marked here by the leading slash in the part number.

EPDM

The rubber used for the cushion liner: it dampens vibration and keeps the metal strap from rubbing what it holds.

Galvanic Corrosion

Corrosion that happens when two different metals touch in a moist environment. The cushion liner acts as a barrier between them.

KMC Stampings

The supplier named by the KMC prefix in the part number.

P21 Item Master

The ERP record for the item: description, classes, documents and history in one place.

PPAP

Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package a supplier submits to prove its process can reliably make a part to print. This item is listed at PPAP Level 4.

RoHS

Restriction of Hazardous Substances — an EU rule limiting materials like lead and mercury in manufactured parts.

VMI (Vendor-Managed Inventory)

A bin system where SBS manages and restocks parts directly at the customer's location. This training module is named after Item D1's cell on the VMI bin card.
